card: Updates the embedded libsecp256k1 subtree to upstream master at commit a0e2e23a71, pulling in 32 upstream pull requests. The update is primarily prompted by new warnings in Clang 24 concerning unsequenced volatile accesses, which were resolved upstream in PR #1998. It also incorporates upstream improvements including relaxed input handling for empty silent payments arrays, secret-clearing cleanups, and expanded constant-time and exhaustive test suites.
changed_since_previous: No code or commit changes; the previous description was generated without patch data.
evidence: "The update is prompted by new warnings introduced in Clang 24. bitcoin-core/secp256k1#1998 fixed them in the secp256k1 subtree." (PR description)

Upstream CHANGELOG: "`secp256k1_silentpayments_recipient_prevouts_summary_create` and `secp256k1_silentpayments_recipient_scan_outputs` now return 0 when called with no input public keys or no taproot outputs, respectively, instead of treating this as an illegal argument (which by default calls `abort()`)."
problem: Clang 24 introduced compiler warnings for unsequenced reads to volatile variables in libsecp256k1's modular inverse code, preventing warning-free builds on newer compiler toolchains. The embedded subtree also lacked upstream fixes for silent payments edge cases and additional constant-time testing coverage.

risk.why: A defect in secp256k1 elliptic curve arithmetic or signature verification could cause a consensus divergence across nodes or compromise private keys.
